quote: How we spend our days is, of course, how we spend our lives.
author: Annie Dillard

quote: Not everything that is faced can be changed, but nothing can be changed until it is faced.
author: James Baldwin
source: As Much Truth As One Can Bear

quote: You wanna fly, you got to give up the shit that weighs you down.
author: Toni Morrison

quote: The most difficult thing is the decision to act, the rest is merely tenacity.
author: Amelia Earhart

quote: We tell ourselves stories in order to live.
author: Joan Didion

quote: Doing nothing often leads to the very best of something.
author: A.A. Milne

quote: For a time I rest in the grace of the world, and am free.
author: Wendell Berry

quote: Your silence will not protect you.
author: Audre Lorde

quote: Attention is the beginning of devotion.
author: Mary Oliver

quote: The trouble is, you think you have time.
author: Jack Kornfield

quote: Almost everything will work again if you unplug it for a few minutes, including you.
author: Anne Lamott

quote: The mountains are calling and I must go.
author: John Muir

quote: Rest is not idleness, and to lie sometimes on the grass under trees on a summer's day, listening to the murmur of the water, or watching the clouds float across the sky, is by no means a waste of time.
author: John Lubbock

quote: Children are not things to be molded, but are people to be unfolded.
author: Jess Lair
source: I Ain't Much, Baby — But I'm All I've Got

quote: How lucky I am to have something that makes saying goodbye so hard.
author: A.A. Milne

quote: You do not rise to the level of your goals. You fall to the level of your systems.
author: James Clear

quote: Somewhere, something incredible is waiting to be known.
author: Carl Sagan

quote: The key is not to prioritize what's on your schedule, but to schedule your priorities.
author: Stephen Covey

quote: The question of what you want to own is actually the question of how you want to live your life.
author: Marie Kondo
source: The Life-Changing Magic of Tidying Up

quote: The good life is a process, not a state of being. It is a direction, not a destination.
author: Carl Rogers
